461:t_1:86.en:
$$梅本$$
「It's to stand together with humans.」

461:t_1:88.en:
$$梅本$$
「Come to think of it, it's only natural. Robots are things built by humans... things built for the sake of humans, after all.」

461:t_1:89.en:
$$梅本$$
「But that doesn't mean using robots as tools you can simply replace when they break...」

461:t_1:90.en:
$$梅本$$
「A real robot is one that stands with humans and shares in their joys and sorrows... something you can call a partner.」

461:t_1:91.en:
$$勝平$$
「Oh, is that all? Then it's not just $$トライダー$$. My $$ザンボット$$ and $$正太郎$$'s $$鉄人$$ are just the same.」

461:t_1:92.en:
$$梅本$$
「Exactly. That's why I decided to help you.」

461:t_1:93.en:
$$正太郎$$
「Are you perhaps talking about back in the $$再世戦争$$?」

461:t_1:94.en:
$$梅本$$
「Yes. Every one of your robots that I saw back then gave me the sense that it shared its pilot's hardships and joys.」

461:t_1:95.en:
$$勝平$$
「...Sorry to say this, Uncle... but isn't that pretty much a given?」

461:t_1:96.en:
$$梅本$$
「That very given had been lost from the $$ロボット帝国$$ of $$ガバール星$$.」

461:t_1:97.en:
$$正太郎$$
「Why? That Mother Computer $$シグマ$$ was also built to improve human lives, wasn't it?」

461:t_1:98.en:
$$梅本$$
「Exactly. But one day... without anyone knowing, $$シグマ$$ was hijacked, and its purpose was changed to the destruction of human civilization.」

461:t_1:101.en:
$$正太郎$$
「$$ガイゾック$$... They're the enemy you and the others fought in the $$ＵＣＷ$$, right?」

461:t_1:102.en:
$$勝平$$
「So how did they end up on $$ガバール星$$ in the $$ＡＤＷ$$?!」

461:t_1:103.en:
$$梅本$$
「$$ガイゾック$$ aims to destroy human civilization... We don't know the whole picture, but it seems they have the power to transfer across parallel worlds, and...」

461:t_1:104.en:
$$梅本$$
「It seems they've been active for hundreds of years... perhaps even thousands, at worst.」

461:t_1:105.en:
$$勝平$$
「So that's why you had the data on $$ザンボット３$$, the robot from $$ビアル星$$, Uncle...」

461:t_1:106.en:
$$正太郎$$
「But why, exactly... does $$ガイゾック$$ try to destroy human civilization?」

461:t_1:107.en:
$$勝平$$
「I fought the $$コンピュータードール#pilot$$ they called a god, but I never really understood its purpose...」

461:t_1:108.en:
$$勝平$$
「All I know is that they said humans are an evil existence...」

461:t_1:109.en:
$$梅本$$
「The $$コンピュータードール#pilot$$ you faced must be a separate one from the one that hijacked $$シグマ$$ on $$ガバール星$$.」

461:t_1:110.en:
$$梅本$$
「But their purpose is the same. They are beings that deny humanity.」

461:t_1:112.en:
$$梅本$$
「That's all I have to say. Is that enough for you, $$金田正太郎$$?」

461:t_1:114.en:
$$梅本$$
「I threw that name away. I'm $$梅本$$ now.」

461:t_1:116.en:
$$梅本$$
「You're an honest boy. I'm sure $$ワッ太$$ is the same.」

461:t_1:117.en:
$$勝平$$
「You bet. He's a straight shooter through and through.」

461:t_1:118.en:
$$梅本$$
「I see. If friends like you say so, then my choice was not a mistake after all.」

461:t_1:119.en:
$$梅本$$
「As a scientist, I did everything I could. Now I'll bet on $$ワッ太$$, to whom I entrusted that power.」

461:t_1:120.en:
$$正太郎$$
「Oh... sorry. I need to take a call on the comm.」

461:t_1:121.en:
$$大塚$$
「Can you hear me, $$正太郎$$? A mysterious robot army has appeared in $$お台場$$. Sortie right away, you too.」

461:t_1:123.en:
$$勝平$$
「Those guys! Did they follow us all the way to $$蒼の地球$$?!」

461:t_1:124.en:
$$正太郎$$
「Sorry, $$梅本$$. We... have to go.」

461:t_1:125.en:
$$梅本$$
「Be careful. I'm praying for your victory.」

461:t_1:126.en:
$$勝平$$
「Don't you need to see $$ワッ太$$, Uncle?」

461:t_1:127.en:
$$梅本$$
「That will be after peace returns to this planet.」

461:t_1:128.en:
$$正太郎$$
「Understood. We'll do our best so that day comes as soon as possible.」

461:t_1:129.en:
$$勝平$$
「Take care of yourself till then, Uncle!」

461:t_1:131.en:
$$梅本$$
($$ガバール星$$... A homeland I can never return to...)

461:t_1:132.en:
$$梅本$$
(But on this Earth, I built something to be proud of.)

461:t_1:133.en:
$$梅本$$
($$竹尾$$... I believe in your sons, and the robots that stand with them.)

461:t_2:4.en:
$$ワッ太$$
「...I see. So $$梅本$$ had a past like that.」

461:t_2:6.en:
$$柿小路$$
「He must have gone through a lot, too.」

461:t_2:7.en:
$$厚井$$
「A homeland he can never return to, huh...」

461:t_2:8.en:
$$勝平$$
「If you can't go back, all you can do is live where you are.」

461:t_2:10.en:
$$勝平$$
「I bet my ancestors were just the same as Uncle $$梅本$$.」

461:t_2:11.en:
$$木下$$
「Your ancestors... you mean the $$ビアル星人$$ who were driven from their homeland.」

461:t_2:12.en:
$$勝平$$
「I'm sure at first, my ancestors missed the homeland they could never go back to, too.」

461:t_2:13.en:
$$勝平$$
「But they lived as Earthlings. That's why their descendants, me and $$宇宙太$$ and $$恵子$$, are here.」

461:t_2:14.en:
$$宇宙太$$
「Your ancestors must have found hope in living on Earth.」

461:t_2:15.en:
$$恵子$$
「$$梅本$$ is the same, then, since he was able to build a real robot like $$トライダー$$.」

461:t_2:16.en:
$$ワッ太$$
「...$$勝平$$... Do you think $$梅本$$ will come to visit me once there's peace...?」

461:t_2:18.en:
$$郁絵$$
「Then, President... our company's policy is settled.」

461:t_2:19.en:
$$ワッ太$$
「Yeah...! With $$トライダー$$ powered up thanks to $$梅本$$, I'll definitely take back peace!」

461:t_2:20.en:
$$ワッ太$$
「And then I'll thank $$梅本$$. For building $$トライダー$$ for our company... thank you, I'll tell him.」

461:t_2:21.en:
$$シンジ$$
(A homeland I can never return to, huh...)

461:t_2:22.en:
$$赤木$$
「$$シンジ$$... Didn't you go out with $n and the others?」

461:t_2:23.en:
$$シンジ$$
「...There's no point in going to $$第２新東京市$$ now, so...」

461:t_2:24.en:
$$赤木$$
「If that's how it is, that's fine.」

461:t_2:26.en:
$$赤木$$
「But, $$シンジ$$... don't ever stop walking.」

461:t_2:27.en:
$$赤木$$
「If you're not going to look back at the past, that's fine. Then keep moving forward.」

461:t_2:28.en:
$$赤木$$
「The past is like a homeland you can never return to. If you can't go back, let's find a new way to live.」

461:t_2:29.en:
$$シンジ$$
「$$赤木$$, is that how you've lived too?」

461:t_2:30.en:
$$赤木$$
「That's how I want to live. ...Whether I'm actually managing it, I can't tell myself.」

461:t_2:33.en:
$$赤木$$
「is an irresponsible thing I won't say.」

461:t_2:34.en:
$$赤木$$
「But nobody knows how it turns out until the result is in. You won't know anything for sure unless you try.」
